definitions.meaning: first meaning: the central mark on a target
second meaning: a hard round peppermint boiled sweet

explanation.walkthrough: The scan's 'Mart' is a misreading of 'Mark'. The surface sounds like someone called Mark being sweet; the 's is just 'is' joining two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of a dartboard or target is called by this name, and so is a striped British boiled candy.

parts.note: surface reading: weak barrels that would break easily
setter's reading: small water barrels carried in a ship's boats, whose name sounds like things that break

explanation.walkthrough: On a ship a breaker is a small cask for drinking water; the clue jokes that fragile things are 'breakers'. Breakers are also large waves, fitting the nautical air.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaker is a small keg kept in a lifeboat for water, a term from sailing usage.

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so these letters come out in an odd arrangement

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl looks oddly sluggish during lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean sluggish and lacking energy, like an animal in hibernation.

indicators.note: something put in another word sits between its letters

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Huge numbers of men were caught up in one particular battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Somme in northern France gave its name to the bloody 1916 battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of the Somme, fought in 1916, is one of the best-known engagements of the First World War.

indicators.note: a recession is a moving back, so the joined words go into reverse

parts.note: with 'for' after it, to look for is to seek
an old word for no

explanation.surface: US citizens hope the economy will not slide back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look for' together means SEEK; 'recession' sounds economic but asks for the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is a common informal name for a person from the United States.

clue.text: Dexterous little publicity trio is replaced

parts.note: an ad is a small advertisement, a little piece of publicity

indicators.note: when something is replaced its letters are put back in different positions, a call to rearrange

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A skilful advertising trio gets swapped out for new people.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone skilful and quick with their hands or mind.

clue.text: Went round about refusal to give up explosive

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the next

parts.note: to rotate is to turn round
a plain refusal

explanation.surface: Someone circled back on refusing to hand over a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give up' sounds like surrendering the bomb, but in a down clue 'up' means the assembled letters are read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the small explosive charge used to set off a larger blast.

parts.note: OK means all right
taken as written
pi is informal British for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: Fine: what a self-righteous creature!
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword favourite for sanctimonious.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest mammal of central Africa, related to the giraffe.

parts.note: surface reading: a helpful person who tells you things
setter's reading: the cashier at a bank counter, whose job title also means one who tells

explanation.walkthrough: One who tells is literally a teller, and a teller is also a bank clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller is the bank employee at the counter who deals with deposits and withdrawals.

clue.text: Russian leader makes mark when about fifty

indicators.note: about means around, so one item encloses the other

parts.note: a stain is a mark
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A Soviet ruler leaves his mark at around fifty years old.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalin led the Soviet Union from the 1920s until his death in 1953.

clue.text: Site meant to be adapted . for a cafe

indicators.note: adapting something reshapes it, so these letters are to be reworked into a new order

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A location intended to be converted into a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop is a printing blemish. ESTAMINET is a French word for a small cafe or bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French cafe selling drinks, a word familiar from the First World War.

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside its letters

parts.note: the end of something, as in the tail end
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A footpath shows up on the right as you reach the end.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside TAIL. The apostrophe before 'end' is a printing stray.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a rough track or footpath across country.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a playing card, which you may turn up when you cut the pack

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' suggests a wound for the villain, but it is cutting a deck of cards, where the jack, also called the knave, may turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Knave is an old word for a scoundrel and also the older British name for the jack in a pack of cards.

clue.text: For instance, a linnet ruined the wild rose

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: seven letters taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A songbird, a linnet say, has spoilt a hedgerow rose.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweet briar, a wild rose of European hedgerows.

clue.text: The right grades are changed in these respects

indicators.note: things that are changed take a new form, so these letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Proper grades have been altered in these particular ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In these respects' and 'in these regards' mean the same, which shows the swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Regards and respects are synonyms both as aspects of a matter and as greetings sent to someone.

parts.note: surface reading: an excellent scheme
setter's reading: literally standing out, a drawing with raised hills and valleys

explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' praises a scheme on the surface; literally it means standing out, and a plan can be a drawn map.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map shows the land's heights as raised surfaces or shading, so its features stand out.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: advance warning, as in giving the answer
second meaning: a sheet pinned up on a noticeboard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on board' suggests boarding a ship; the board is a pinboard on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Notice is formal warning of something, and also a posted announcement displayed for all to read.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman takes vehicle to go abroad, nothing more

parts.note: a taxi
aller is French for to go, so it is the foreign word
zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A Spanish gent hails a taxi to leave the country, and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' asks for the word in another language: French aller.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is Spanish for a gentleman, originally a horseman or knight.

clue.text: Envy possession of new drug — ask East about it

indicators.note: going about something surrounds it, so the outer pieces wrap around the rest
something new is remade, so these letters are formed afresh

parts.note: to beg is to ask
taken as written, then rearranged
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Jealous of someone holding a new drug, you ask an Easterner about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge someone something is to resent their having it, which is to envy them.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: musical runs of notes practised up and down
second meaning: the small plates covering a fish's skin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots of notes' hints at banknotes; it means musical exercises a pianist plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both graded runs of musical pitches and the overlapping horny plates on a fish's body.

clue.text: She's on the right lines, providing wine

parts.note: taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right
Ry is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A woman doing things properly offers a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: RY for railway is a crossword convention; 'on the right lines' sounds like doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from the Jerez region of southern Spain.

clue.text: Story of ARP organisation taken to island retreat

indicators.note: organising something puts it into a new order, so these three letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so this word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's first exile

explanation.surface: A tale of the Air Raid Precautions service evacuated to a hideaway on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: ARP was Britain's wartime Air Raid Precautions organisation; 'retreat' looks like a noun meaning hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short moral tale, like those told in the Gospels.

indicators.note: a thing between two others sits inside them, flanked on both sides

parts.note: the Po of Italy and the Ure of Yorkshire
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A coach road running between two rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' looks like a vehicle, fitting 'way'; it means how a person holds their body.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage in the sense of bearing means the way one holds oneself, which is posture.

clue.text: Raising problem in a spirit of hostility?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it upward, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bringing up a difficulty in a hostile mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue drops the 'a' that the wordplay needs. Animus is Latin for mind or spirit, and in English means ill will.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is a feeling of hostility or ill will towards someone.

clue.text: Little Oliver East knows a. sculptor

parts.note: Noll is a pet form of Oliver, as in 'Old Noll' for Cromwell
E is the compass abbreviation for East
to ken is Scots and northern English for to know

explanation.surface: A boy called Oliver from the east is acquainted with an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stop after 'a' is a printing stray. Joseph Nollekens was an eighteenth-century English sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Nollekens was a celebrated London sculptor of portrait busts in the Georgian era.

indicators.note: something confounded is thrown into confusion, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then scrambled

explanation.surface: A Bennet sister grumbles about her wretched everyday routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bennet sisters are Jane, Elizabeth, Mary, Kitty and Lydia in Austen's Pride and Prejudice; the stray apostrophe is a printing blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is the youngest Bennet daughter, who elopes with Wickham in Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Happy-looking chap, but a non-starter, this runner

indicators.note: a non-starter never begins, so the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: someone with a grin on his face

explanation.surface: A cheerful-looking fellow who sadly never gets going in his race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-starter' sounds like a horse that misses a race, which suits the runner, but it removes the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A miler is an athlete or horse that specialises in races over one mile.

indicators.note: to obscure something is to hide it from view, so a letter is taken out of sight

parts.note: middle-aged split into its two parts, middle and age
taken as the letter to remove; this part of the printed clue is hard to account for

explanation.surface: An insect that flies alongside a mysterious mountaineer in later life.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer comes from MID-AGE losing its A, but 'climber' does not clearly give A, so the clue as printed may be garbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny two-winged fly, often found swarming near water.

indicators.note: a word that comes back as itself reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: a polite title for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman is sent home on her own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned by herself' reads like travelling home alone; here it says the word is the same written back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a respectful form of address for a woman, so it stands for 'she'.

parts.note: a round is a single shot fired
the head is the principal, as of a school

explanation.surface: A senior member of parliament has been shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundheads were supporters of Parliament in the English Civil War, so the definition is historical rather than a modern MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundheads, named for their cropped hair, fought for Parliament against the Royalist Cavaliers in the 1640s.

clue.text: Notes from an instrument on board

indicators.note: being on a vessel means being inside it, so one item goes within the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one goes on board
a plucked string instrument

explanation.surface: A tune heard from a musical instrument played aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: HARP sits inside SS. 'On board' meaning inside SS is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharps are notes raised a semitone, marked with the hash-like sign on a stave.

clue.text: This girl might appear short of coin

definitions.text: This girl might appear short of coin

parts.words: This girl might appear short of coin
parts.note: surface reading: a young woman who is broke
setter's reading: her name, shortened, is the name of a small copper coin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of coin' looks like penniless; it means the name in short form is a coin. Penny was a British coin, and a common short form of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl's name is commonly shortened to Penny, which is also a small coin, so she 'appears' as one.
